what_ours_does: Measures a draft against a locally-fitted idiolect before it is sent. Five parts, and they are not one component: (1) voice_engine.py, a hashed character n-gram TF-IDF embedding, PCA-whitened, fitted on the local WhatsApp corpus, numpy the sole dependency; (2) profiles.py, per-surface metric rule sets (blog_post, devto, x) fitted with voice.py fit; (3) voice_score.py, percentile bands and a k-NN centrality score placing a draft inside or outside the corpus distribution; (4) lexicon/, spell check over 370,105 English words and a 324,329-entry Hebrew lexicon built from hspell 1.4; (5) voice_engine.separate_speakers, kept ONLY so a negative result stays reproducible, documented in its own module docstring.
why:
The embedding is the part an off-the-shelf tool wins, and I am saying so rather than defending all 1,408 lines. voice_engine.py hand-rolls hashed character n-gram TF-IDF plus PCA whitening in 293 lines; scikit-learn's TfidfVectorizer(analyzer='char_wb') into TruncatedSVD is the same construction, better tested, and roughly five lines. The only thing standing against the swap is a stated repo constraint rather than a capability gap: this component declares numpy as its sole dependency, and sklearn is a large addition to a skill that ships inside ~/.claude. Note what does NOT save it: the module docstring rejects pretrained encoders on two grounds, that they embed meaning rather than idiolect and that hosted ones ship private message content off the machine, and the second ground does not apply to sklearn at all, which is local. So the honest position is that the embedding survives on dependency budget, not on merit, and that is a weaker argument than the file currently makes for itself.

What genuinely does not exist off the shelf is the rest. No listed tool fits a per-surface metric profile from a private corpus and reports a draft's percentile against it; the tools below check text against a general standard of good writing, which is a different question from whether it sounds like one specific person. The Hebrew leg is also load-bearing and unserved: the corpus is Hebrew/English code-switched, and none of the alternatives carries a Hebrew lexicon of this shape.

The honest counterweight is that a corpus-fitted 1,408-line stylometer is a large instrument for a gate whose output is advisory, and the speaker-separation negative result means every per-contact number it reports is thread-level, both sides combined, not one writer's. That limitation is documented in the code and must be repeated wherever the numbers are cited.

alternatives.name: scikit-learn
alternatives.covers: TfidfVectorizer(analyzer='char_wb') plus TruncatedSVD reproduces voice_engine.py's whole construction: character n-gram TF-IDF followed by a whitening projection, with cosine k-NN on top for the centrality score. This is the strongest alternative and it covers the single largest file in the component.
alternatives.gap: Covers the embedding and nothing else: no per-surface rule fitting, no percentile bands, no Hebrew lexicon, no hard-fail list. Adds a large dependency to a component that declares numpy as its only one, and to a skill tree that is copied into ~/.claude.

alternatives.name: language-tool-python
alternatives.covers: Grammar, style and spell checking against LanguageTool's rule sets, local Java server or hosted API, Python and CLI interfaces. Overlaps the lexicon/ spell-check leg.
alternatives.gap: Checks text against a general standard of correctness, not against one person's measured distribution, which is this component's entire purpose. GPL-3.0-only, and the local mode needs a Java runtime, which nothing else in this repo requires. The hosted mode would send private message content off the machine, which the component's own docstring rules out.
alternatives.cost: Free, GPL-3.0-only, pip install language-tool-python; local mode pulls a Java LanguageTool server.

alternatives.name: textdescriptives
alternatives.covers: Readability formulas (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid, SMOG) and stylometric features (token length statistics, dependency distance, part-of-speech proportions, syllable counts, semantic coherence) as spaCy v3 pipeline components. Overlaps the descriptive-statistics half of profiles.py.
alternatives.gap: Computes features, not a fitted target: there is no corpus percentile, no per-surface rule set, and no notion of a draft being inside or outside one writer's distribution. Requires spaCy plus a downloaded language model, and Hebrew support would have to be verified separately.
alternatives.cost: Free, Apache-2.0, pip install textdescriptives; needs spaCy and a model.

alternatives.name: Dedicated stylometry toolkits (PyStyl, Fast Stylometry, StyloMetrix, stylometry-python)
alternatives.covers: Authorship attribution from character n-gram features, which is the same statistical family as voice_engine.py. PyStyl is an experimental Python port of Duquesne University's JGAAP.
alternatives.gap: Built to answer 'which of these candidates wrote this', not 'how far is this draft from the target distribution', and none of them writes the per-surface rule sets the prose gates consume. UNVERIFIED, and stated as such: I did not establish current version or maintenance status for any of these four, so this row is a pointer for the recheck rather than evidence.
alternatives.maturity: NOT ESTABLISHED. A web search on 2026-07-31 surfaced all four but returned no maintenance or release evidence for JGAAP or PyStyl.

evidence: PyPI JSON API for scikit-learn, language-tool-python and textdescriptives fetched 2026-07-31; versions, licenses and summaries above are quoted from those responses, not recalled.

Read dot-claude/skills/voice-metrics/voice_engine.py:1-40 (module docstring) and voice_score.py for the feature list; the character n-gram TF-IDF plus PCA-whitening construction and the numpy-only dependency claim are the file's own words.
wc -l over the component: 1,408 lines across seven Python files, voice_engine.py the largest at 293.
wc -l over lexicon/: 370,105 English words, 324,329 Hebrew entries.

NOT verified: whether LanguageTool or textdescriptives support Hebrew to a usable standard, and the maintenance status of the four stylometry toolkits. Both would change the verdict's shape and neither was checked.
recheck: Re-run if the numpy-only dependency constraint is dropped for this skill, since that is the only thing keeping voice_engine.py against scikit-learn. Also re-run if the speaker-direction problem is ever solved, because per-contact statistics would stop being thread-level and the component's value would change materially.
strongest_counterargument: The dependency-budget defence is thin. If a session ever installs scikit-learn into ~/.claude for any other reason, voice_engine.py loses its last argument and should be deleted in favour of five lines, which would take the component from 1,408 lines to about 1,100 with better-tested math underneath.
